title: U.S. House · South Carolina's 7th District
area: South Carolina's 7th Congressional District (Myrtle Beach/Pee Dee region)

context.text: Both major-party primaries were canceled after only one candidate filed in each: incumbent Russell Fry (R) and John Vincent (D) each advanced without a primary contest.

candidates.name: Russell Fry
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced without a primary after the Republican primary was canceled

positions.summary: His campaign site calls for strengthening immigration law, ending catch-and-release and deporting criminal illegal aliens.
positions.quote: STRENGTHEN immigration law, END catch-and-release, and DEPORT criminal illegal aliens.

positions.summary: His campaign site says he will champion school choice and let education dollars follow the student.
positions.quote: Champion school choice and let education dollars follow the student.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (Energy; Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Communications and Technology subcommittees) and the House Judiciary Committee (Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement; Courts, Intellectual Property, and the Internet subcommittees), per his official House website (119th Congress, 2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: Ballotpedia's profile for Fry lists only 2023-2024 committee assignments (Judiciary and Oversight and Government Reform); his official House website shows different, current 2025-2026 assignments (Energy and Commerce and Judiciary), used instead. No current-cycle stated positions were located within the research budget. Key floor votes and FEC totals are added separately by script.

candidates.name: John Vincent
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced without a primary after the Democratic primary was canceled

priorities.text: Fighting wasteful federal spending while protecting vital programs, and supporting increased border security alongside what he calls a fair immigration system.
Championing tax relief for working families, job creation through community-college partnerships, cutting red tape for small businesses, and making healthcare more affordable.
As a Navy veteran, improving VA healthcare, expanding veterans' housing programs, and enhancing education and job-training benefits for veterans.

positions.summary: His campaign platform says he will work to pass the War Powers Resolution so Congress can rein in the current war.
positions.quote: Work with all members of Congress to pass the War Powers Resolution so Congress can reel in this unconstitutional war

positions.summary: His campaign platform says he will work with Congress to end global tariffs.
positions.quote: Work with all members of Congress to end global tariffs.

positions.summary: His fiscal policy backgrounder proposes raising the top individual income tax rate to 39.6% for high incomes.
positions.quote: Return the top marginal individual income tax rate from 37% to 39.6% for taxable income above $400,000 (single) / $450,000 (married filing jointly).

positions.summary: His SAVE Act policy backgrounder states he opposes the act and its documentary requirements.
positions.quote: that right should not be burdened by unnecessary, costly, and discriminatory documentary requirements

positions.summary: His education policy backgrounder criticizes South Carolina's school voucher program.
positions.quote: misguided, scandal-plagued school voucher program that drains hundreds of millions of dollars away from the children and communities who need public schools the most

statements.quote: provide low-cost insurance for every American who chooses it, without eliminating private insurance and without adding one dollar to the debt
statements.context: On his campaign policy page, describing his planned ALL American Healthcare Act

statements.quote: A gradually rising fee on fossil fuel companies ($40–50/ton, rising $5–10/year).
statements.context: In his National Fiscal Policy backgrounder, describing a carbon fee and dividend

statements.quote: Rather than proposing an entirely new federal program, John Vincent advocates building on existing, proven frameworks for maximum achievability.
statements.context: In his National Fiscal Policy backgrounder

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements come from his campaign website policy page and policy backgrounders (PDFs, March-April 2026), accessed Oct. 19, 2026, plus his 2025 Ballotpedia survey. The backgrounders are campaign-authored documents. No stated position found on abortion, guns, immigration enforcement, or transgender sports.

researchNotes: Basic-tier research. A Republican write-in candidate (Branden Brown) appears on Ballotpedia's general-election list but is not included as a full entry; per the research division of labor, Fry's federal key floor votes and FEC totals are left for later automated addition. Public biographical detail on John Vincent is limited to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; his birth year and Navy service dates were not found.
